DA

device-auth-system-advanced

A login that recognizes the device before anyone types a password. The server identifies the caller by network identity first, then a password confirms it, so a login is bound to one specific device.

  • Device identity resolved server-side only, so it can't be spoofed from a request
  • BCrypt password hashing and stateless JWT sessions
  • 5-attempt login lockout
  • React
  • Spring Boot 3
  • Spring Security
  • PostgreSQL
  • JWT
2F

Shotfolio two-factor authentication

Two-factor login that I added to a photography marketplace platform I'm building. Scan a QR code once, then a fresh 6-digit code is needed on every sign-in. It runs on the standard TOTP algorithm (RFC 6238).

  • Sign-in takes two steps: a correct password returns a 5-minute challenge token, and real tokens are issued only after the code is verified
  • 8 one-time backup codes, stored only as SHA-256 hashes
  • A used code can't be replayed, and codes are compared in constant time with room for clock drift
  • Java
  • Spring Boot
  • HMAC-SHA1 (RFC 6238)
  • SHA-256
  • JWT
  • PostgreSQL

      How Java keeps my apps secure

      Pick a request and watch it travel through the layers of a Spring Boot backend. Each attack is stopped by the layer built for it.

      Memory safetyArrays are bounds-checked and the JVM manages memory, which rules out the buffer overflows behind many classic attacks.
      Spring SecurityOne filter chain guards every request, so sign-in and roles are enforced in one place.
      Built-in cryptoSecureRandom, MessageDigest and constant-time comparison for hashing and checking codes safely.

      How WordPress plugins make a site better

      Pick a situation and watch it travel through WordPress. A plugin steps in at the hook built for the job, so the site gets faster, safer and smarter without touching WordPress itself.

      Faster sitesPage caching, lazy-loading and minification cut load time, which helps visitors stay and search rankings improve.
      Safer sitesLogin lockouts, nonce and capability checks and prepared queries stop bots and forged requests before they do harm.
      Features on demandHooks and filters add fees tracking, backups or dashboards without editing core files, so updates never break them.
